newsitem.title: USA: Food price rise will be limited - USDA's Glickman.
newsitem.headline: Food price rise will be limited - USDA's Glickman.

text.p: Food price increases will not go up very much, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Friday, adding consumers have little to worry about.
"We've said it's going to be up some but not materially, no cataclysmic or catastrophic rise in food prices," Glickman told reporters.
Labor Department figures released earlier in the day showed that food prices last month were 3.6 percent higher than in August 1995 and were up 0.4 percent from a month ago.
The Agriculture Department has forecast a food price increase of 2.8 to three precent this year.
Food prices have been affected by higher milk prices and higher-priced feed, which affects meat production.
"I think these numbers are reflecting a little tighter supplies out there for a lot of products but nothing the economy can't handle," Glickman said.

For 1997, the Agriculture Department has forecast food price increases of three to four percent. It might mean food prices that climb faster than the overall U.S. inflation rate for the first time this decade.
